According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple has prepared multiple new features for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, which should be more appealing to health-conscious users. The company is reportedly also testing two finishes for the rumored ceramic version.

Brand New Health Feature Upgrades

If you've always felt that the Apple Watch's fitness tracking features were less than ideal, the following two major health feature upgrades should pique your interest. The two new features are: all-day heart rate tracking, and a completely redesigned application interface that makes it easier to extract useful health data. Here's Gurman's description of the new application:

As a current WHOOP user, I can say that the main reason this product retains me is that the WHOOP application makes it easier to extract useful information from health data. It shows me all the factors affecting sleep or recovery, but when using the Apple Watch, it feels like only the three "Activity" rings matter. If Apple makes substantial progress in this area, I would be very happy.

One of the keys to enriching the Apple Watch data experience is having more data. Apple is reportedly testing enabling the heart rate sensor to continuously record throughout the day, rather than only during exercise or at random times.

Two Brand New Finishes

We've previously heard that Apple is considering using ceramic material for the Apple Watch Series 12, and Gurman is now reporting that there will be two color options: traditional white, and dark gray. At launch, there will also be "a few new band colors and combinations."

Future Design Overhaul

The current Apple Watch design language can be traced back to the Apple Watch Series 10 in 2024. That was a relatively modest change—the company made the watch thinner, but at the cost of slightly larger bezels. According to Bloomberg, we may see a brand new Apple Watch design with the Series 11 next year, though it's also possible it could be delayed until the Series 12:

I'm really looking forward to seeing Apple's next design move. They seem to have reached the ceiling of the rounded design language, so perhaps we'll see a completely new form factor. Hopefully, it won't affect backward compatibility with older bands.
